mount.description: Mount the grid with all the rows (data already in memory). "Visible" = from setState to the end of the first frame committed with the whole viewport (first/last visible row and column) showing the right content. "Settled" = until the first frame committed after the grid's last DOM mutation. Memory is the JS heap retained by the grid after GC (heap after mount - heap before mount).

sort-string.description: Click the "code" column header (string column, unique-ish values) - first click sorts ascending (cold), second click descending. Measured from pointerdown to the end of the first frame committed with all visible rows sorted (and each row consistent: its cells belong to the same data row).

metrics.label: Ascending: click to sorted rows painted
Descending: click to sorted rows painted

sort-number.description: Click the "salary" column header (number column, unique-ish values) - first click sorts ascending (cold), second click descending. Measured from pointerdown to the end of the first frame committed with all visible rows sorted (and each row consistent: its cells belong to the same data row).

metrics.label: Ascending: click to sorted rows painted
Descending: click to sorted rows painted

scroll-jump.description: Programmatic jumps to 10 far-away scroll positions (like dragging the scrollbar thumb). Measured from setting scrollTop to the end of the first frame committed with the first and last visible rows showing the right content, at the right position.

metrics.label: Jump to rows painted (median of jumps)

scroll-vertical.description: Wheel-scroll down 24000px at 8000px/s (Input.synthesizeScrollGesture - real input pipeline, same gesture for every grid). Frame outcomes come from Chrome's compositor (PipelineReporter): "partial" = frame shown without the main thread's update, "dropped" = no new frame. rAF frame intervals and Long Animation Frames come from the page.

scroll-horizontal.description: Wheel-scroll right/left over all columns, 4 sweeps at 4000px/s (Input.synthesizeScrollGesture - real input pipeline, same gesture for every grid). Frame outcomes come from Chrome's compositor (PipelineReporter): "partial" = frame shown without the main thread's update, "dropped" = no new frame. rAF frame intervals and Long Animation Frames come from the page.

correctness-vertical.description: Same kind of vertical wheel gesture, faster (20000px/s). After every painted frame, samples points across the body and checks the cell there is the one that should be there for the current scroll position: "blank" = no cell, "wrong" = a cell for another row/column (stale content, or position lagging behind the scroll). This is the main thread's view of the frame; it reads layout, so it is never combined with the timing passes.

correctness-horizontal.description: Same kind of horizontal wheel gesture. After every painted frame, samples points across the body and checks the cell there is the one that should be there for the current scroll position: "blank" = no cell, "wrong" = a cell for another row/column (stale content, or position lagging behind the scroll). This is the main thread's view of the frame; it reads layout, so it is never combined with the timing passes.

visual-blank-vertical.description: Fast vertical wheel gesture (20000px/s) while recording what the compositor actually displays (CDP screencast). Each frame is checked for blank areas: vertical runs of the body with no text where rows should be. Unlike the correctness probe, this also catches the compositor scrolling ahead of the main thread. Screencast capture skips frames under load and adds overhead - compare the grids, not absolute numbers.

updates-low.description: Live updates, low frequency. The grid shows the rows in the order of the data. 10 updates of 1,000 random rows each, one at a time: each update is sent 500 ms after the previous one is painted. An update changes salary, bonus, hours, score (by up to ±1%) in new copies of the rows: random rows, plus all the rows in the viewport, so that every update changes what is on screen. Every grid gets the same updates, through the API it documents for changing rows. Measured from sending the update to the end of the first frame committed with the viewport showing it (the right rows, with the new values, in the right order).

metrics.label: Update to rows painted (median of updates)

updates-low-sorted.description: Live updates, low frequency. The grid shows sorted by salary, highest first - the updates change the salaries, so rows move. 10 updates of 1,000 random rows each, one at a time: each update is sent 500 ms after the previous one is painted. An update changes salary, bonus, hours, score (by up to ±1%) in new copies of the rows: random rows, plus all the rows in the viewport, so that every update changes what is on screen. Every grid gets the same updates, through the API it documents for changing rows. Measured from sending the update to the end of the first frame committed with the viewport showing it (the right rows, with the new values, in the right order).

metrics.label: Update to rows painted (median of updates)

updates-low-filtered.description: Live updates, low frequency. The grid shows filtered to a salary of at least 115,000 (about half of the rows) - the updates change the salaries, so rows go in and out of the filter. 10 updates of 1,000 random rows each, one at a time: each update is sent 500 ms after the previous one is painted. An update changes salary, bonus, hours, score (by up to ±1%) in new copies of the rows: random rows, plus all the rows in the viewport, so that every update changes what is on screen. Every grid gets the same updates, through the API it documents for changing rows. Measured from sending the update to the end of the first frame committed with the viewport showing it (the right rows, with the new values, in the right order).

metrics.label: Update to rows painted (median of updates)

updates-low-grouped.description: Live updates, low frequency. The grid shows grouped by department (10 collapsed groups), with the sum of the salaries of each group - the updates change the salaries, so the sums change. 10 updates of 1,000 random rows each, one at a time: each update is sent 500 ms after the previous one is painted. An update changes salary, bonus, hours, score (by up to ±1%) in new copies of the rows: random rows, plus all the rows in the viewport, so that every update changes what is on screen. Every grid gets the same updates, through the API it documents for changing rows. Measured from sending the update to the end of the first frame committed with the viewport showing it (the right rows, with the new values, in the right order).

metrics.label: Update to rows painted (median of updates)

updates-high.description: Live updates, high frequency. The grid shows the rows in the order of the data. A feed of 50 updates a second, of 100 random rows each, for 4 s (200 updates). An update changes salary, bonus, hours, score (by up to ±1%) in new copies of the rows: random rows, plus all the rows in the viewport, so that every update changes what is on screen. Every grid gets the same updates, through the API it documents for changing rows. The page hands the grid the updates once per animation frame: all the ones that arrived since the previous frame, as one update - so a grid that keeps the main thread busy gets them later, and more at once. "Lag at the end" = from the arrival of the last update to the end of the first frame committed with the viewport showing it. "Update delay" = from the arrival of an update to the frame that hands it to the grid. Frames, gaps and blocking time come from the trace, from the first update until the last one is painted: the frames the main thread committed, and the part over 50 ms of every task.

metrics.label: Lag at the end: last update to painted
